Non-uniform dependence on initial data for the 2D viscous shallow water equations

Jinlu Li Affiliation:  School of Mathematics and Computer Sciences, Gannan Normal University, Ganzhou 341000, China    Yanghai Yu Note: E-mail: lijinlu@gnnu.edu.cn; yuyanghai214@sina.com(Corresponding author); mathzwp2010@163.com Affiliation:  School of Mathematics and Statistics, Anhui Normal University, Wuhu 241002, China    Weipeng Zhu Affiliation:  School of Mathematics and Information Science, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou 510006, China
August 24, 2026

 

Abstract: The failure of uniform dependence on the data is an interesting property of classical solution for a hyperbolic system. In this paper, we consider the solution map of the Cauchy problem to the 2D viscous shallow water equations which is a hyperbolic-parabolic system. We prove that the solution map of this problem is not uniformly continuous in Sobolev spaces Hs×HsH^{s}\times H^{s} for s>2s>2.

Keywords: Shallow water equations; Non-uniform dependence; Sobolev spaces.

MSC (2010): 35Q35; 35A01; 76N10

 

1 Introduction

The 2D viscous shallow water equations are given by the following system, which have systematically introduced in [2, 3]

{∂tρ+div⁡(ρ​u)=0,∂t(ρu)+div(ρu⊗u)−μdiv(ρ∇u)+ρ∇ρ=0,ρ|t=0=ρ0,u|t=0=u0.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}\rho+\mathrm{div}(\rho u)=0,\\ \partial_{t}(\rho u)+\mathrm{div}(\rho u\otimes u)-\mu\mathrm{div}(\rho\nabla u)+\rho\nabla\rho=0,\\ \rho|_{t=0}=\rho_{0},\;u|_{t=0}=u_{0}.\end{array}\right.

where ρ⁡(x,t)\rho(x,t) is the height of fluid surface, u⁡(x,t)u(x,t) is the horizontal velocity field and μ>0\mu>0 is the viscous coefficient. We suppose that the initial data ρ0​(x)\rho_{0}(x) is a small perturbation of some positive constant ρ¯0\overline{\rho}_{0}.

Classical solutions and well-posedness of the initial (boundary) value problem for the shallow water equations (1) have been studied extensively. By using Lagrangian coordinates and Hölder space estimates, Bui [1] obtained the local existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the Cauchy-Dirichlet problem for (1) with initial data in C2+αC^{2+\alpha}. With the help of the energy method of Matsumura and Nishida [33], Kloeden [26] and Sundbye [34] independently showed the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the Cauchy-Dirichlet problem for (1). Subsequently, Sundbye [35] also proved the existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem for (1) using the method of [33]. Due to the strong nonlinearity of system (1), the problem of existence of solutions for large initial data is difficult. By applying the Littlewood-Paley decomposition theory for Sobolev spaces to obtain a losing energy estimate in HsH^{s} for any s>2s>2, Wang–Xu [36] obtained local solutions for any initial data and global solutions to (1) for small initial data (u0,ρ0−ρ¯0)∈Hs×Hs(u_{0},\rho_{0}-\bar{\rho}_{0})\in H^{s}\times H^{s} with s>2s>2. Liu–Yin [30, 31, 32] improved the result of [36] in the Sobolev spaces with low regularity and inhomogeneous Besov spaces. Chen–Miao–Zhang [6] obtained the local well-posedness of system (1) for general initial data in critical LpL^{p} type Besov spaces with 1≤p<41\leq p<4 by developing a new method which relies on the smoothing properties of the heat equations. Recently, Li–Hong–Zhu [28] proved that the system (1) is ill-posed in the critical Besov spaces with p>4p>4.

The continuous dependence is particularly important when PDEs are used to model phenomena in the natural world since measurements are always associated with errors. One of the first results of this type was proved by Kato [27] who showed that the solution operator for the (inviscid) Burgers equation is not Hölder continuous in the Hs​(𝕋)H^{s}(\mathbb{T})-norm (s>3/2)(s>3/2) for any Hölder exponent. After the phenomenon of non-uniform continuity for some dispersive equations was studied by Kenig et al. [24], many results with regard to the non-uniform dependence on the initial data have been obtained for other nonlinear PDEs including the Euler equations [18], the Camassa-Holm equation [19, 20, 29], the Benjamin-Ono equation [25], the compressible gas dynamics [21, 23], the Hunter-Saxton equation [22] and so on. Nevertheless we notice that almost the above system mentioned is hyperbolic. As stated in [23], the exhibition of nonuniform behavior in a hyperbolic system related to the incompressible system indicates that the nonuniform dependence is hyperbolic in nature. From the PDE’s point of view, classical solution is uniform dependence on the data for a parabolic system. Naturally, one may wonder if uniform dependence on the data of solution for a coupled system which is hyperbolic-parabolic can persist or not.

In this paper, we focus on the 2D viscous shallow water equations

{∂tρ+div⁡(ρ​u)=0,∂t(ρu)+div(ρu⊗u)−μdiv(2ρ𝔻u)+ρ∇ρ=0,ρ|t=0=ρ0,u|t=0=u0.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}\rho+\mathrm{div}(\rho u)=0,\\ \partial_{t}(\rho u)+\mathrm{div}(\rho u\otimes u)-\mu\mathrm{div}(2\rho\mathbb{D}u)+\rho\nabla\rho=0,\\ \rho|_{t=0}=\rho_{0},\;u|_{t=0}=u_{0}.\end{array}\right.

where the strain tensor 𝔻​u=12​(∇u+∇𝖳u)\mathbb{D}u=\frac{1}{2}(\nabla u+\nabla^{\mathsf{T}}u) is the symmetric part of the velocity gradient.

For the sake of convenience, we take ρ¯0=1\bar{\rho}_{0}=1 and denote ϱ=ρ−1\varrho=\rho-1, we can reformulate the system (1) equivalently as follows

{∂tϱ+div​u+u⋅∇ϱ=−ϱ​div​u,∂tu−μΔu−μ∇divu+u⋅∇u+∇ϱ=2∇(ln(1+ϱ))⋅𝔻u,ϱ|t=0=ϱ0,u|t=0=u0.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}\varrho+\mathrm{div}u+u\cdot\nabla\varrho=-\varrho\mathrm{div}u,\\ \partial_{t}u-{\mu}\Delta u-{\mu}\nabla\mathrm{div}u+u\cdot\nabla u+\nabla\varrho=2\nabla(\ln(1+\varrho))\cdot\mathbb{D}u,\\ \varrho|_{t=0}=\varrho_{0},\;u|_{t=0}=u_{0}.\end{array}\right.

Roughly speaking, the system (1) can be regarded as a special case of compressible Navier-Stokes equations (see Refs. [6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17] and the references therein). We emphasize that the equations (1) form a quasi-linear hyperbolic-parabolic system and possess strong nonlinear terms. Although the system (1) is partially parabolic, owing to the first equation of (1) which is of hyperbolic type, this creates the possibility of the non-uniformity for the solution map. In this paper, we prove the failure of uniform dependence on the data for (1). To the best of our knowledge, it allows us to give a first kind of answer to the problem of the non-uniform dependence on the data for the 2D viscous shallow water equations.

Our main result of this paper is stated:

Theorem 1.1 (Nonuniform dependence on initial data)

Let s>2s>2. The data-to-solution map (u0,ϱ0)↦(u⁡(t),ϱ⁡(t))(u_{0},\varrho_{0})\mapsto\big(u(t),\varrho(t)\big) of the Cauchy problem (1) is not uniformly continuous from any bounded subset in Hs×HsH^{s}\times H^{s} into 𝒞⁡([0,T],Hs×Hs)\mathcal{C}([0,T];H^{s}\times H^{s}), namely, there exists two sequences of solutions (u1,n​(t),ϱ1,n​(t))\big(u_{1,n}(t),\varrho_{1,n}(t)\big) and (u2,n​(t),ϱ2,n​(t))\big(u_{2,n}(t),\varrho_{2,n}(t)\big) such that

(C.1)

∥u1,n,ϱ1,n∥Hs+∥u2,n,ϱ2,n∥Hs≲1;\|u_{1,n},\varrho_{1,n}\|_{H^{s}}+\|u_{2,n},\varrho_{2,n}\|_{H^{s}}\lesssim 1;

(C.2)

limn→∞(‖u2,n​(0)−u1,n​(0)‖Hs+‖ϱ2,n​(0)−ϱ1,n​(0)‖Hs)=0;\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\big(\|{u}_{2,n}(0)-u_{1,n}(0)\|_{H^{s}}+\|\varrho_{2,n}(0)-\varrho_{1,n}(0)\|_{H^{s}}\big)=0;

(C.3)

lim infn→∞(‖u2,n​(t)−u1,n​(t)‖Hs+‖ϱ2,n​(t)−ϱ1,n​(t)‖Hs)≳t\liminf\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}\big(\|u_{2,n}(t)-u_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}+\|\varrho_{2,n}(t)-\varrho_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}\big)\gtrsim t

for any t∈[0,T0]t\in[0,T_{0}] with small time T0T_{0}.

Remark 1.1

It should be mentioned that most non-uniformity results for solutions to other nonlinear PDEs were obtained by the Himonas-Misiołek construction in [18]. The method we used in proving Theorem 1.1 is motivated by [29] and is completely different from that [18].

Remark 1.2

We note that the local well-posedness result holds for s>1s>1. However, the restriction on s>2s>2 is essential in the present paper.

Outline of the proof to Theorem 1.1 There are two key points in proving Theorem 1.1:

  • •

    On one hand, we construct one sequence of initial data (u1,n​(0),ϱ1,n​(0))=(0,fn)(u_{1,n}(0),\varrho_{1,n}(0))=(0,f_{n}), which leads to the solutions (u1,n​(t),ϱ1,n​(t))(u_{1,n}(t),\varrho_{1,n}(t)) to (1) and (u1,nap,ϱ1,nap)(u^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n},\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n}) to the linearized system (2.3) respectively. Based on the special choice of fnf_{n}, we can prove the distance between the real solution (u1,n​(t),ϱ1,n​(t))(u_{1,n}(t),\varrho_{1,n}(t)) and the approximate solution (u1,nap,ϱ1,nap)(u^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n},\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n}) will tends to zero in HsH^{s} as n→∞n\to\infty . See Propositions 3.1.

  • •

    On the other hand, we construct another sequence of initial data (u2,n​(0),ϱ2,n​(0))=(gn,fn)(u_{2,n}(0),\varrho_{2,n}(0))=(g_{n},f_{n}), which leads to the solutions (u2,n​(t),ϱ2,n​(t))(u_{2,n}(t),\varrho_{2,n}(t)) to (1) and (u2,nap,ϱ2,nap)(u^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n},\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}) to the linearized system (2.3) respectively. Next, we aim to show that the mentioned solution (u2,nap,ϱ2,nap)(u^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n},\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}) cannot approximate the real solution (u2,n​(t),ϱ2,n​(t))(u_{2,n}(t),\varrho_{2,n}(t)). For more details, see Propositions 3.2.

Combining the precious steps, we can conclude that the distance of two solution maps at the initial time is converging to zero, while at any later time it is bounded below by a positive constant, which means the solution maps are not uniformly continuous.
The structure of the paper In Section 2 we recall some notations and known results which will be used in the sequel. Also, we investigate the spectrum properties of the linearized system corresponding to (1), which will play a crucial role in the construction of approximate solutions. In Section 3 we prove Theorem 1.1 based on the well-posedness result and some key error estimates. In Section 4 we present some details in the computations.

3 Proof of Theorem 1.1

This section is devoted to proving Theorem 1.1. We begin with the well-posedness result for (1). For the details of the proof, we refer to [30, 31, 36].

3.1 Global Well-posedness

Lemma 3.1

Assume that s>2s>2. For any initial data (u0,ϱ0)(u_{0},\varrho_{0}) which belongs to

BR={(ψ,ϕ)∈Hs×Hs:‖ψ‖Hs+‖ϕ‖Hs≤c}for small​c>0,B_{R}=\big\{(\psi,\phi)\in H^{s}\times H^{s}:\|\psi\|_{H^{s}}+\|\phi\|_{H^{s}}\leq c\big\}\quad\text{for small}\;c>0,

then System (1) has a unique global solution (u(t),ϱ(t))∈𝒞([0,+∞);Hs×Hs)\big(u(t),\varrho(t)\big)\in\mathcal{C}([0,+\infty);H^{s}\times H^{s}).
Moreover, we have the solution size estimate

∥u(t)∥Hσ+∥ϱ(t)∥Hσ≤C∥u0,ϱ0∥Hσfor allσ≥s.\displaystyle\|u(t)\|_{H^{\sigma}}+\|\varrho(t)\|_{H^{\sigma}}\leq C\|u_{0},\varrho_{0}\|_{H^{\sigma}}\quad\text{for all}\;\sigma\geq s. (3.29)

3.2 Approximate Solutions

Let ϕ^∈𝒞0∞​(ℝ)\widehat{\phi}\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}_{0}(\mathbb{R}) be an even, real-valued and non-negative function on ℝ\mathbb{R} and satisfy

ϕ^​(ξ)=\displaystyle\widehat{\phi}(\xi)= 1,\displaystyle 1, if |ξ|≤14|\xi|\leq\frac{1}{4},
ϕ^​(ξ)=\displaystyle\widehat{\phi}(\xi)= 0,\displaystyle 0, if |ξ|≥12|\xi|\geq\frac{1}{2}.

Let (ui,nap,ϱi,nap)(u^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n},\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n}) (i=1,2i=1,2) be the solution of the following equation

{∂tϱi,nap+div​ui,nap=0,∂tuapi,n−μΔuapi,n−μ∇divuapi,n+∇ϱapi,n=0,\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n}+\mathrm{div}u^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n}=0,\\ \partial_{t}u^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n}-\mu\Delta u^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n}-\mu\nabla\mathrm{div}u^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n}+\nabla\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{i,n}=0,\\ \end{array}\right.

3.4 Non-uniform Continuous Dependence

With Propositions 3.1–3.2 in hand, we can prove Theorem 1.1.

Behavior at time t=0t=0. Obviously, we have

‖u2,n​(0)−u1,n​(0)‖Hs+‖ϱ2,n​(0)−ϱ1,n​(0)‖Hs=‖gn‖Hs≤C​2−n,\displaystyle\|{u}_{2,n}(0)-u_{1,n}(0)\|_{H^{s}}+\|\varrho_{2,n}(0)-\varrho_{1,n}(0)\|_{H^{s}}=\|g_{n}\|_{H^{s}}\leq C2^{-n},

which means that the condition (𝐂​.2)(\bf{C.2}) in Theorem 1.1 holds.

Behavior at time t>0t>0. Notice that

u2,n−u1,n=u2,ner−u1,ner+u2,nap−u1,nap,\displaystyle u_{2,n}-u_{1,n}=u^{\rm{er}}_{2,n}-u^{\rm{er}}_{1,n}+u^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}-u^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n},
ϱ2,n−ϱ1,n=t​Vnap+ϱ2,ner−ϱ1,ner+ϱ2,nap−ϱ1,nap,\displaystyle\varrho_{2,n}-\varrho_{1,n}=t{V}_{n}^{\rm{ap}}+\varrho^{\rm{er}}_{2,n}-\varrho^{\rm{er}}_{1,n}+\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}-\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n},

by the triangle inequality and Propositions 3.1 and 3.2, we deduce that for t≤1t\leq 1

‖ϱ2,n​(t)−ϱ1,n​(t)‖Hs+‖u2,n​(t)−u1,n​(t)‖Hs\displaystyle\|\varrho_{2,n}(t)-\varrho_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}+\|u_{2,n}(t)-u_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}
≥\displaystyle\geq t∥Vnap∥Hs−(∥u2,nap−u1,nap∥Hs+∥ϱ2,nap−ϱ1,nap∥Hs)−(∥u1,ner,ϱ1,ner∥Hs+∥u2,ner,ϱ2,ner∥Hs)\displaystyle~t\|V^{\rm{ap}}_{n}\|_{H^{s}}-\big(\|u^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}-u^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n}\|_{H^{s}}+\|\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}-\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n}\|_{H^{s}}\big)-\big(\|u^{\rm{er}}_{1,n},\varrho^{\rm{er}}_{1,n}\|_{H^{s}}+\|u^{\rm{er}}_{2,n},\varrho^{\rm{er}}_{2,n}\|_{H^{s}}\big)
≳\displaystyle\gtrsim t​‖Vnap‖Hs−2−n−2−n2​min⁡{εs,1}−2−n​min⁡{εs,1}−t32,\displaystyle~t\|V^{\rm{ap}}_{n}\|_{H^{s}}-2^{-n}-2^{-\frac{n}{2}\min\{\varepsilon_{s},1\}}-2^{-n\min\{\varepsilon_{s},1\}}-t^{\frac{3}{2}}, (3.61)

where we have used

‖u2,nap−u1,nap‖Hs2+‖ϱ2,nap−ϱ1,nap‖Hs2≲‖gn‖Hs2≲2−2​n.\|u^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}-u^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n}\|^{2}_{H^{s}}+\|\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{2,n}-\varrho^{\rm{ap}}_{1,n}\|^{2}_{H^{s}}\lesssim\|g_{n}\|^{2}_{H^{s}}\lesssim 2^{-2n}.

Notice that −Vnap=u2,nap⋅∇ϱ2,nap-V^{\rm{ap}}_{n}=u_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}\cdot\nabla\varrho_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}, we decompose it as

−Vnap=(u2,nap)1​∂1ϱ2,nap+(u2,nap)2​∂2ϱ2,nap=(gn)1​∂1fn+E,\displaystyle-V^{\rm{ap}}_{n}=(u_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}})_{1}\partial_{1}\varrho_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}+(u_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}})_{2}\partial_{2}\varrho_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}=(g_{n})_{1}\partial_{1}f_{n}+E,

where

E:=(u2,nap−gn)1​∂1ϱ2,nap+(gn)1​∂1(ϱ2,nap−fn)+(u2,nap)2​∂2ϱ2,nap.E:=(u_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}-g_{n})_{1}\partial_{1}\varrho_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}+(g_{n})_{1}\partial_{1}(\varrho_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}-f_{n})+(u_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}})_{2}\partial_{2}\varrho_{2,n}^{\rm{ap}}.

For more details of proof, see A.3 in Section 4.

Furthermore, (3.61) reduces to

‖ϱ2,n​(t)−ϱ1,n​(t)‖Hs+‖u2,n​(t)−u1,n​(t)‖Hs≳t​‖(gn)1​∂1fn‖Hs−2−n2​min⁡{εs,1}−t32,\displaystyle\|\varrho_{2,n}(t)-\varrho_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}+\|u_{2,n}(t)-u_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}\gtrsim t\|(g_{n})_{1}\partial_{1}f_{n}\|_{H^{s}}-2^{-\frac{n}{2}\min\{\varepsilon_{s},1\}}-t^{\frac{3}{2}}, (3.63)

combining the following estimate whose proof is postponed to A.4 in Section 4

lim infn→∞‖(gn)1​∂1fn‖Hs≳‖ϕ′​ϕ‖L22​‖ϕ2‖L2,\displaystyle\liminf_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|(g_{n})_{1}\partial_{1}f_{n}\|_{H^{s}}\gtrsim\|\phi^{\prime}\phi\|^{2}_{L^{2}}\|\phi^{2}\|_{L^{2}}, (3.64)

we get from (3.63) that

lim infn→∞(‖ϱ2,n​(t)−ϱ1,n​(t)‖Hs+‖u2,n​(t)−u1,n​(t)‖Hs)≳tfor​t​small enough,\displaystyle\liminf_{n\rightarrow\infty}\big(\|\varrho_{2,n}(t)-\varrho_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}+\|u_{2,n}(t)-u_{1,n}(t)\|_{H^{s}}\big)\gtrsim t\quad\text{for}\ t\ \text{small enough},

which is nothing but the condition (𝐂​.3)(\bf{C.3}) in Theorem 1.1.

Thus, we complete the proof of Theorem 1.1.

2​cos2⁡(2n​x1)=1−cos⁡(2n+1​x1),2\cos^{2}(2^{n}x_{1})=1-\cos(2^{n+1}x_{1}),

we have

‖ϕ′​(x1)​ϕ​(x1)​cos⁡(2n​x1)‖L22=12​‖ϕ′​(x1)​ϕ​(x1)‖L22−12​∫ℝ|ϕ′​(x1)​ϕ​(x1)|2​cos⁡(2n+1​x1)​d​x1,\|\phi^{\prime}(x_{1})\phi(x_{1})\cos(2^{n}x_{1})\|^{2}_{L^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\|\phi^{\prime}(x_{1})\phi(x_{1})\|^{2}_{L^{2}}-\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\phi^{\prime}(x_{1})\phi(x_{1})|^{2}\cos(2^{n+1}x_{1})\mathrm{d}x_{1},

which follows from Riemann-Lebesgue’s Theorem that

limn→∞‖ϕ′​(x1)​ϕ​(x1)​cos⁡(2n​x1)‖L22=12​‖ϕ′​(x1)​ϕ​(x1)‖L22.\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\|\phi^{\prime}(x_{1})\phi(x_{1})\cos(2^{n}x_{1})\|^{2}_{L^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\|\phi^{\prime}(x_{1})\phi(x_{1})\|^{2}_{L^{2}}. (4.3)

Combining (4.2) and (4.3) yields the desired (3.64).
